sentences.text: In 1883, French engineer Léon Charles Thévenin proved that any linear two-terminal circuit of resistors and sources can be replaced by an equivalent circuit consisting of a single voltage source VTh in series with a resistor RTh.
Similarly, Norton's theorem proves the same network can be replaced by an equivalent current source IN in parallel with a resistor RN.
VTh is the open-circuit voltage across terminals a-b. IN is the short-circuit current flowing when a-b are connected.
The equivalent resistance is RTh = Voc / Isc.
